findings.title: V2 `canManage()` returns true for a VIEW-only all-groups grant, so `POST /groups` can create or move top-level groups
findings.description: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` (lines 65-71) ends with `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. A null group id falls back to the "Groups" type resource, so any caller with an all-groups VIEW grant passes. The no-argument `canManage()` is what `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` checks through `auth.groups().requireManage()` (`GroupsResource.java:181`). That path then calls `realm.createGroup` (line 202). When the body carries an existing group id, it calls `realm.moveGroup(child, null)` (line 198), which has no per-group manage check. The `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` Javadoc says V2 includes VIEW, so this is documented behavior. It still lets a read-only grant change the group hierarchy. V1 is not affected, because `GroupPermissions.canManage()` (lines 274-276) checks only `MANAGE_USERS`.

findings.title: V2 `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` adds resource UUIDs instead of group IDs, so all-groups view-members holders see zero users
findings.description:
Line 123 adds `groupResource.getId()`, which is the store-generated resource UUID (`JPAResourceStore.java:66`). The group id is the resource name (`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:109,118-121`). V1 correctly strips the prefix from the name (`GroupPermissions.java:315`). The set is stored as `UserModel.GROUPS` (`UsersResource.java:448-451`) and matched against `UserGroupMembershipEntity.groupId` (`JpaUserProvider.java:1070`).

For a caller with an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS grant, the lookup at line 122 falls back to the "Groups" type resource and passes. The set then contains that resource's UUID, which matches no membership row. The list (`UsersResource.java:453`) and the count (`UsersResource.java:398,425,430`) return nothing, even though `canViewMembers` (`GroupPermissionsV2.java:83-87`) would allow those members. `BruteForceUsersResource.java:147` has the same pattern.

Corrected IDs alone would not be enough. The list query's subquery (`JpaUserProvider.java:1081`) also requires a resource named `group.resource.<groupId>`, which is the V1 naming scheme. V2 never creates that name. This is outside the diff, but this change is what routes V2 into that query.

findings.title: A group's own V2 resource hides the all-groups grant, so all-groups VIEW/MANAGE is ignored for any group with a per-group grant
findings.description:
`hasPermission` looks up the group's own resource at line 141 and falls back to the "Groups" type resource only when that resource is absent (line 143). When another admin holds a per-group grant on group G, evaluation runs only against G's resource. That resource is untyped (`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:118-128` never calls `setType`), so `DefaultPolicyEvaluator.java:73-74` skips the type-level policy lookup.

The all-groups policy is attached to the type resource (`AuthorizationProvider.java:323-326`). It therefore does not come back from `findByResource(G)`, and it does not come back from the null-resource scope lookup, because `findPolicyIdByNullResourceScope` requires `pe.resources is empty` (`PolicyEntity.java:62`).

As a result, `canView(G)`, `canManage(G)`, `canViewMembers(G)` and `canManageMembership(G)` return false for an admin whose all-groups grant should apply. `GroupsResource.java:113` then hides G from listings, and `GroupResource.java:176-179` rejects sub-group listing. `UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission` (lines 105-114) uses the same lookup shape but is not part of this diff.

findings.title: V2 group-specific view grants are missing from the group set because group resources are never typed `Groups`, so the user count returns 0
findings.description:
`getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` enumerates with `findByType(server, "Groups")` (line 121). Group-specific resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (lines 118-128) without a type, and `JPAResourceStore.create` does not set one either. Only the realm-wide "Groups" resource is typed (`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:273-274`), so per-group grants never enter the set.

For a caller whose only grant is VIEW_MEMBERS on one group, the set is empty. `UsersResource.getUsersCount` (line 430) then calls the empty-set overload, which returns 0 immediately (`JpaUserProvider.java:599-601`). The count is 0, while the list falls back to per-user checks and returns the member. That fallback also paginates in SQL (`JpaUserProvider.java:773`) before the per-user filter (`UsersResource.java:460`), so permitted members outside the first page are never returned. Typing group resources at creation would fix this enumeration, and it shares a root cause with the shadowing defect above.
